## Loading this week's release

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import networkx as nx
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

%matplotlib inline

# TODO: load this week's data, e.g.
nodes = pd.read_csv("data/week1_nodes.tsv", sep="\t", comment="#", quoting=3)
edges = pd.read_csv("data/week1_edges.tsv", sep="\t", comment="#", names=["source", "target"])

graph = nx.DiGraph()
graph.add_nodes_from(nodes.node_id)
graph.add_edges_from(edges.itertuples(index=False))

name_lookup = dict(zip(nodes.node_id, nodes.name))
```

## Analysis

### Popularity

Investigating the counts of degrees in the graph, we notice a tail, especially for the in-degrees.

```{python}
#| label: In and Out Degrees
#| fig-cap: In and Out Degrees

in_degrees = graph.in_degree
out_degrees = graph.out_degree

max_degree = max(list(in_degrees) + list(out_degrees), key=lambda degree: degree[1])[1]
degrees = pd.Series(range(1, max_degree+2))

# Convert in_degrees and out_degrees to pandas Series
in_degrees_series = pd.Series([degree[1] for degree in in_degrees]) +1
out_degrees_series = pd.Series([degree[1] for degree in out_degrees]) +1

# Count occurrences of each degree
in_degrees_count = in_degrees_series.value_counts().sort_index().reindex(degrees, fill_value=0)
out_degrees_count = out_degrees_series.value_counts().sort_index().reindex(degrees, fill_value=0)

plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))

plt.plot(in_degrees_count, label="In-degrees")
plt.plot(out_degrees_count, label="Out-degrees")
plt.title("In-degree and Out-degree Distribution", fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel("Degree", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Number of nodes", fontsize=12)

plt.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

```

```{python}
#| label: logarithms1
#| fig-cap: In and Out Degrees with log relations
log_in_degrees_count = in_degrees_count.apply(np.log10)
log_out_degrees_count = out_degrees_count.apply(np.log10)
log_degrees = degrees.apply(np.log10)
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))

plt.plot(log_in_degrees_count, label="Log-In-degrees-Count")
plt.plot(log_out_degrees_count, label="Log-Out-degrees-Count")
plt.title("In-degree and Out-degree Distribution", fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel("Degree", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Log(Number of nodes)", fontsize=12)
plt.legend()
plt.show()

```

```{python}
#| label: logarithms2
#| fig-cap: In and Out Degrees with log relations
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))

plt.plot(log_degrees, in_degrees_count, label="Log-In-degrees-Count")
plt.plot(log_degrees, out_degrees_count, label="Log-Out-degrees-Count")
plt.title("In-degree and Out-degree Distribution", fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel("Log(Degree)", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Log(Number of nodes)", fontsize=12)
plt.legend()

```

### The team nobody links to

9 characters are totally cut off from the rest of the graph — linked to each other, but zero
links in or out to anyone else.

```{python}
undirected = graph.to_undirected()
components = sorted(nx.connected_components(undirected), key=len, reverse=True)

giant = components[0]
island = max(components[1:], key=len)
isolates = {n for comp in components[1:] for n in comp if len(comp) == 1}

print(f"giant component: {len(giant)} characters")
print(f"cut-off team: {len(island)} characters")
print(f"true isolates (no links at all): {len(isolates)} characters")
```

```{python}
for node_id in sorted(island, key=lambda x: name_lookup[x]):
    print(f"  {name_lookup[node_id]}")
```

All nine are from *Strikeforce: Morituri*, a 1980s spin-off team. Same Marvel-characters
category as Spider-Man, and yet not one link either way.

```{python}
#| label: fig-island
#| fig-cap: "Strikeforce: Morituri (red) vs. everyone else (grey) — completely disconnected from the rest of the network."

non_isolate_nodes = [n for n in undirected.nodes() if undirected.degree(n) > 0]
sub = undirected.subgraph(non_isolate_nodes)
pos = nx.spring_layout(sub, seed=42, k=0.2)

main_extent = max(abs(c) for xy in pos.values() for c in xy)
ring_radius = main_extent * 1.6
for i, node_id in enumerate(sorted(isolates)):
    angle = 2 * np.pi * i / len(isolates)
    pos[node_id] = (ring_radius * np.cos(angle), ring_radius * np.sin(angle))

node_colors = ["#c8102e" if n in island else "#d9d9d9" for n in undirected.nodes()]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 9))
nx.draw_networkx_edges(sub, pos, alpha=0.1, edge_color="lightgray", ax=ax)
nx.draw_networkx_nodes(undirected, pos, node_color=node_colors, node_size=40, linewidths=0, ax=ax)
ax.axis("off")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## What surprised us

We didn't expect the network to have a total dead zone, but it does: the 9-person
[Strikeforce: Morituri](https://marvel.fandom.com/wiki/Strikeforce_Morituri_(Earth-1287)) team
links to each other and literally nobody else.

Turns out there's a real reason. Morituri was never part of the mainstream Marvel universe —
it's a standalone late-80s sci-fi series set on an alternate Earth (retroactively tagged
Earth-1287), about humans fighting off an alien invasion by taking a process that gives them
powers but kills them within a year. Spider-Man and the X-Men live in a completely different
continuity, so there was never really a reason for their wiki pages to cross-link. The one
crossover Morituri ever got (an X-Force story) happened decades later and clearly wasn't enough
to leave a trace in this graph.
